channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Moraes vota para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata Amaral
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to convict former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against congresswoman Tabata Amaral, proposing a sentence of one year detention and 39 day-fines (over R$80,000) over a 2021 social media post alleging her bill on intimate pads served a company lobby. The vote noted the crime was committed against a public official due to her functions and via social media with vast reach, and stated that alternative penalties cannot apply as Bolsonaro is in an unknown location (USA).

item.title: Lula: afrouxamento das regras de posses de armas levou a desvios que beneficiaram criminosos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the loosening of gun ownership rules in Brazil, stating that it benefited criminals. He said those who relaxed the regulations now want to 'outsource' the fight against organized crime to other countries, without directly naming the Bolsonaro administration.

item.title: Lula sacrifica debate do fim da escala 6×1 ao fazer populismo eleitoral com a proposta
item.description: Lula proposed ending the 6×1 work scale as an electoral strategy to reverse declining popularity, despite knowing it has little chance of passing Congress due to the election year, sectoral resistance, and legal risks. The proposal, criticized by experts and entities like the CNI, could raise business costs, increase unemployment, and push workers into informal labor without wage compensation. Lula will likely blame Congress and 'elites' for the failure, maintaining a 'us vs. them' narrative to mobilize his base.

item.title: Na Espanha, Lula critica big techs e fala em “colonialismo digital”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized big tech companies in Barcelona, warning that without regulation, they are creating a 'digital colonialism' by extracting and monetizing data to concentrate power in the hands of a few billionaires. He called for expanding platform regulation, citing the ECA Digital as a first step, and stressed the need to protect Brazil’s sovereignty, especially during an election year, to prevent foreign interference. Lula also announced bilateral cooperation with Spain on supercomputing and AI, and condemned the 'industry of lies,' including hate speech and disinformation online.

item.title: ‘Tenho muita preocupação no Brasil para me preocupar com a Venezuela’, diz Lula na Espanha
item.description: President Lula stated during the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit in Barcelona that Brazil should not directly interfere in Venezuela's political affairs, emphasizing that his focus remains on domestic challenges. He defended respect for Venezuelan sovereignty, asserting that Venezuelans themselves must decide their country's future, including whether to call elections, and said the Brazilian government does not seek a leading role in the process. While avoiding intervention, Lula expressed a desire for stability and well-being in Venezuela, reaffirming Brazil's principle of non-intervention in international crises.

item.title: Lula diz que afrouxamento das regras de posse de armas levou a desvios que beneficiaram criminosos
item.description: President Lula stated that the loosening of gun possession rules in Brazil, enacted during Bolsonaro's government, led to deviations that benefited criminals. He criticized those who promoted the measure and now seek to outsource the fight against organized crime to other countries, referencing the U.S. initiative to label factions like PCC and CV as terrorist organizations. Lula also noted that the number of progressive leaders worldwide is declining, during his participation in the Democracy Always Forum in Spain.

item.title: Lula diz que fará acordo sobre minerais críticos com todos os países que quiserem negociar com o Brasil
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will establish agreements on critical minerals with all countries willing to cooperate, announcing a partnership with Spain on rare earths. He emphasized the defense of national sovereignty over mineral wealth, declaring that no one will own Brazil’s mineral resources. Lula also defended Venezuela’s right to self-determination, asserting that its political future should be decided solely by Venezuelans.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro sobem o tom nas redes com IA, memes e ataques diretos
item.description: The electoral dispute between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is already operating with full campaign logic on social media, using AI, memes, and direct attacks. The PT invested R$ 378,000 in content boosting in April, focusing on linking Flávio to scandals like Banco Master and the Bolsonaro family, while Bolsonaro’s allies shared an AI-generated video linking Lula and his son to INSS suspicions. The escalation occurs without formal TSE restrictions, but with continuous production and narrative warfare.

item.title: Alckmin diverge de Lula e defende manutenção da taxa das blusinhas
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin defended the maintenance of the 'tax on small clothing items', stating there are no planned changes and that the tax protects Brazilian companies from unfair competition with imported goods. He diverged from President Lula and Minister José Guimarães, who advocate ending the tax, arguing it is necessary to balance the tax burden between domestic industry and imports. The tax, which applies to international purchases under $50, has caused political backlash among middle- and low-income consumers.

item.title: ‘Precisamos regular tudo o que for digital’, diz Lula em cúpula na Espanha
item.description: President Lula advocated for expanded regulation of digital platforms and social media during the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit, arguing that the virtual world must follow the same rules as the physical world to combat misinformation, hate, and violence. He criticized big tech companies for extracting and monetizing user data, likening their actions to 'digital colonialism,' and stressed the need for international cooperation to counter disinformation factories, especially during electoral periods. Lula also referenced existing measures, such as banning cell phones in schools and expressing concern over the growth of online betting.

item.title: A resposta de Alessandro Vieira ao pedido de investigação feito contra ele por Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) requested the Attorney General's Office to dismiss the criminal complaint filed by Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, following Vieira's inclusion of Mendes in the final report draft of the Organized Crime CPI on charges of responsibility crime. The proposal was rejected by the CPI committee by a 6-4 vote, and Vieira argues no crime occurred since no formal act was consummated, and that legislators enjoy immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their mandate. He claims Mendes is applying the law selectively and that STF jurisprudence protects his actions in the CPI.

item.title: Lula afirma que regulamentação das redes digitais é prioridade
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced that Brazil will implement new regulations for digital platforms in 2026, an election year, to protect democracy, national sovereignty, and counter what he calls 'digital neocolonialism' by big techs. He also stressed the need to regulate online betting sites (bets) due to their role in increasing household indebtedness, arguing that lack of oversight causes social and economic harm.

item.title: Brasil e Espanha assinam atos na 1ª Cúpula Brasil-Espanha
item.description: Brazil and Spain signed seven agreements during the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit in Barcelona, including memoranda of understanding on social and solidarity economy, critical minerals, racial and gender equality, science and technology, culture, and social security. Negotiations were also concluded on public policies for SMEs, air transport, and technology. President Lula’s Europe trip includes stops in Spain and Germany, with expectations of over 30 agreements and announcements.

item.title: 'Quando o povo toma uma decisão, temos que aceitar o resultado', diz Lula sobre Flávio
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told German magazine Der Spiegel that, regardless of the outcome of the October 2026 elections, the people's decision must be accepted, even if Senator Flávio Bolsonaro wins. He stressed the importance of respecting the democratic process.

item.title: Alguns se acham mais Bolsonaro que o próprio Bolsonaro, diz Nikolas
item.description: Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) stated that some people consider themselves 'more Bolsonaro than Bolsonaro himself', criticizing exclusionary tendencies within the bolsonarist movement. He denied starting fights with Eduardo Bolsonaro, describing the April exchange as a 'unilateral attack' and reaffirmed his loyalty to the former president, saying his role is that of an 'attacker' in defending Bolsonaro's ideas.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Ministros do governo exemplificam a busca por melhorar a popularidade de Lula
item.description: The Lula government is working to boost the president's popularity ahead of the 2026 re-election bid, with ministers across departments adopting strategies to counter negative narratives. The economic team justifies the prolonged primary deficit by blaming the Bolsonaro administration and projects a surplus only in 2027, while the Justice Ministry highlights anti-crime operations and the new Institutional Relations Minister defends revoking the unpopular 'blusinhas' tax — a move quickly rebuked by Vice President Alckmin.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: 47% defendem convocação de Neymar e 45% são contra, diz pesquisa
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows Brazilian fans divided on Neymar's potential 2026 World Cup call-up: 47% support, 45% oppose, and 8% undecided. Support is stronger in the Northeast and Center-West/North, while the South leans against; the Southeast is evenly split. Lower-income groups show a technical tie, and higher-income brackets slightly favor inclusion.

item.title: Lula defende ampliar regulação das redes sociais para evitar 'intromissão' externa em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for expanding regulation of social media to prevent foreign interference in the electoral year, emphasizing the need to ensure Brazil's digital sovereignty. He noted that the digital ECA was only the first step and further regulations will follow, while also criticizing the 6x1 work schedule and calling for its end to guarantee two days of weekly rest.

item.title: PL da Dosimetria: Motta defende derrubada de veto para liberar presos e 'distensionar' relações com STF
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, Hugo Motta, advocates for overturning the presidential veto on the Dosimetria Bill, which would reduce sentences for those involved in the January 8 coup attempt, aiming to 'ease tensions' between Congress and the STF. He stated the move could lead to the release of approximately 280 individuals detained over the events, potentially benefiting figures like former President Jair Bolsonaro, with the STF responsible for individual sentence reviews.

item.title: Motta diz que não vai 'procrastinar' debate sobre fim da escala 6x1 e prevê votação semana que vem na CCJ da Câmara
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta stated he will not delay the debate on ending the 6x1 work schedule and expects the proposal to be voted on in the CCJ next week. He chose the PEC route to ensure deeper discussion and congressional autonomy, rejecting the government's suggestion to use a constitutionally urgent bill. Motta aims to bring the PEC to the floor this semester, targeting approval by late May or early June to pressure the government to withdraw its own proposal.

item.title: Lula da Silva respalda a Pedro Sánchez en su “no a la guerra”
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva explicitly supported Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's 'no to war' stance during the first Spain-Brazil Summit in Barcelona. Lula said he understood Sánchez's position amid a new global arms race, expressing concern over rising military expenditures. Sánchez emphasized that Brazil and Spain share a worldview grounded in democracy, international cooperation, respect for international law, human rights, and peace.

item.title: Processo de impeachment de Dilma Rousseff, aberto há exatos 10 anos, salvou o PT do colapso total
item.description: The impeachment of Dilma Rousseff, opened exactly 10 years ago, was a constitutional necessity to address Brazil’s severe economic and political crisis, marked by recession, inflation, unemployment and loss of congressional control. Although the PT labeled it a coup, the impeachment had broad public support and was driven by legislators like Bruno Araújo and Mendonça Filho, with Jair Bolsonaro acting only as a bystander, not driving the process. Despite criticizing the impeachment, the PT never ceased defending Dilma personally, while seeking to shift blame for economic failures onto her successors, Temer and Bolsonaro.

item.title: Crusoé: Quem é o melhor vice para Flávio, segundo Nikolas
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) stated that Romeu Zema (Novo), former governor of Minas Gerais, is the best vice-presidential candidate for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 election. According to Ferreira, Zema 'aggregates the most so far' and adds electoral strength, noting that Minas Gerais is Brazil's second-largest electoral college.

item.title: Motta diz que governo avaliou mal texto de PL dos apps
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta claimed the federal government misjudged the text of the bill regulating app-based work, citing a lack of understanding of its political and economic limits. He warned that overregulation could raise platform costs, harm workers, and face opposition in the Chamber, which would not approve a measure with such consequences. Motta emphasized that, despite the disagreement, the pursuit of workers' rights continues, highlighting the 6x1 work scale as a legislative priority for 2026.

item.title: A preocupação da cúpula militar do governo, diante do risco de Flávio Bolsonaro derrotar Lula
item.description: The paper reveals that the military's concern about Lula potentially losing to Flávio Bolsonaro stems from the risk of renewed military involvement in elections and civilian posts—a pattern that enabled past coup plots. If Flávio wins, the previous coup scheme could repeat. Hence, urgent passage of a PEC barring active-duty military from political participation is urged.

item.title: Caixa desiste de lançar casa de aposta em 2026
item.description: Caixa Econômica Federal abandoned plans to launch its betting house in 2026 due to resistance from President Lula and allies, despite having already paid R$30 million for the federal license. The project was postponed to 2027 or canceled following pressure from the PT, which introduced a bill to ban fixed-odds betting in Brazil, labeling it a public health issue. Lula and Haddad advocated for closing or strictly regulating betting firms, while the Health Minister called the idea 'speculation'.

item.title: Líderes de esquerda se reúnem na Espanha em mobilização contra a extrema-direita
item.description: Left-wing leaders, including Pedro Sánchez and Lula, are meeting in Barcelona to mobilize against the far-right and defend multilateralism, in response to Trump’s policies and the rise of the right in Europe. The gathering includes presidents from South Africa and Mexico, aiming to produce a joint declaration on democracy and green transition.

item.title: Brasil teve 1.149 mortes em conflitos no campo desde 1996
item.description: Since 1996, Brazil has recorded 1,149 deaths in rural conflicts, averaging one death every 10 days, according to the CPT. The Eldorado do Carajás massacre in 1996 marked the beginning, and 2017 saw the highest number of fatalities (74). The MST denounces land concentration and the expansion of agribusiness over traditional peoples' territories.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de reunião da 1ª Cúpula Brasil-Espanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is attending the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit in Barcelona, launching a six-day European tour that also includes Germany and Portugal. Prior to the plenary session, he met with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and is expected to sign bilateral agreements, address the press, and meet with business leaders from both nations. The visit is part of an agenda involving 14 ministers and approximately 30 pending agreements.

item.title: Médico de Lula, Roberto Kalil é eleito membro da Academia Nacional de Medicina
item.description: Cardiologist Roberto Kalil Filho, personal physician to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, was elected to the Medicine Section of the National Academy of Medicine (ANM), taking over Seat No. 1 previously held by José Manoel Jansen. Kalil celebrated the election as the fulfillment of a dream and reaffirmed his commitment to advancing medicine and contributing to health policy debates in Brazil.

item.title: Bolsonaristas buscam junto a interlocutores de Trump retomada da Lei Magnitsky contra Moraes
item.description: Allies of Jair Bolsonaro are engaging with individuals linked to Donald Trump to seek the reapplication of the Magnitsky Act against Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, aiming to ultimately impeach Supreme Court justices. The sanctions, which were imposed in 2025 and later lifted, are described as a 'financial death penalty' and were originally based on allegations of influencing Bolsonaro’s trial, which led to his 27-year sentence for coup plotting. Paulo Figueiredo, close to Eduardo Bolsonaro and based in the U.S., says there is no expectation of renewed trade tariffs from Trump, but rather a push for individual sanctions against Brazilian officials.

item.title: “Não é uma briga, é ataque unilateral”, diz Nikolas sobre Eduardo
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) denied having a feud with former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, stating that the criticism he receives is a unilateral attack due to his lack of support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential bid. He said he never instigated a conflict and has been constantly pressured by Eduardo over his stance.

item.title: 'Temos que aceitar', diz Lula sobre eventual vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro na eleição
item.description: Lula said he would accept the election results even if Flávio Bolsonaro wins, emphasizing respect for the people's choice and confidence in Brazil's democracy. He avoided confirming his re-election bid but stated he is preparing physically and politically to run. Lula also criticized global authoritarianism and advocated for a more inclusive UN, asserting that right-wing ideologies spreading hatred have no future.

item.title: Cunha celebra 10 anos do impeachment de Dilma na Câmara
item.description: Former Chamber of Deputies president Eduardo Cunha celebrated the tenth anniversary of the session that accepted the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff, emphasizing that the vote took place under his presidency and resulted in 367 votes in favor of admitting the process.

item.title: O plano de Flávio Bolsonaro para tirar eleitores católicos de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign has identified the Catholic electorate as its primary battleground for 2026, recognizing that despite ideological alignments with this conservative religious group, Lula currently leads among them. The strategy involves increased attendance at Mass, appearances with priests, events with Catholic leaders, and speeches tailored to religious interests, following a perception that the Bolsonaro family has overly focused on evangelical leaders while neglecting Catholic engagement.

item.title: Lula abre giro europeu com Sánchez na Espanha para ampliar agenda bilateral e 'defender democracia'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is attending the 1st Brazil-Spain Summit in Barcelona, co-chaired by Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, focusing on economy, science, technology, culture, and gender equality. The meeting aims to strengthen bilateral ties and defend democracy.

item.title: Lula vai usar saúde como trunfo contra Flávio Bolsonaro, mas estratégia tem riscos
item.description: Lula and his government plan to use health as a central theme in the 2026 re-election campaign, contrasting his administration with Jair Bolsonaro’s during the pandemic, emphasizing improved vaccination rates, access to specialists, and national production of medicines. The strategy aims to link Flávio Bolsonaro to a potential rollback in health policies and the threat of Brazil withdrawing from international organizations like WHO and PAHO, leveraging fear of a Bolsonarist return to power.

item.title: Lula é recebido por Pedro Sánchez em cerimônia oficial, na Espanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was received by Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez in an official ceremony in Barcelona, marking the opening of the 1st Spain-Brazil Summit. The meeting reinforced the bilateral agenda with a focus on political and economic cooperation, including support for the Mercosul-European Union agreement. Lula will remain in Spain until Saturday, when he will participate in a forum on defending democracy against extremism.

item.title: Como o governo está simplificando o processo de emissão de documentos em 2026
item.description: The Brazilian government is simplifying document issuance in 2026 through integrated digital platforms, unified digital identity, and more accessible service channels. The reform goes beyond mere digitization, emphasizing system interoperability and reducing bureaucratic hurdles for citizens.

item.title: Detido nos EUA, Ramagem vê em xeque um sonho que embalou os bolsonaristas: o exílio seguro
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency (Abin) and convicted to 16 years in prison by the STF for his role in the 2022-2023 coup plot, was arrested in Florida by ICE after overstaying a tourist visa. He is awaiting a U.S. decision on his asylum request and Brazil’s extradition demand, while his allies deny the arrest is politically motivated, claiming it was merely a traffic violation. His detention reveals the false belief among Bolsonarist fugitives that they would be safe in right-wing governed countries.

item.title: Governo Lula lança guia que ensina “linguagem não sexista”
item.description: The Lula government launched the Public Communication Guide for Gender Equality, produced by the Ministry of Women, advocating for non-sexist language in public administration to combat inequality and patriarchy. The 54-page document, part of the Brazil Pact against Femicide, argues that all state communication is inherently political and neutrality is impossible. It provides examples such as replacing 'citizens' with 'population' and using 'good morning to everyone and all'.

item.title: Nunes Marques poupa governador de RR com base em informação errada
item.description: TSE Minister Nunes Marques voted to keep Roraima Governor Edilson Damião in office based on false information, claiming he was not part of the government between 2021 and 2022, despite records showing he served as State Secretary of Infrastructure during that period. The trial over the 2022 elected ticket’s cassation for political and economic abuse of power was suspended after a view request by Minister Estela Aranha. Rapporteur Minister Isabel Gallotti had voted for annulment, citing illegal social programs launched during the election year without prior budgetary execution.

item.title: Dez anos do impeachment de Dilma: por onde andam principais envolvidos
item.description: Ten years after the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff, many of the key figures involved remain active in Brazilian politics. Michel Temer, her vice president who succeeded her, is sidelined from electoral races due to Lava Jato convictions, while authors of the impeachment request like Hélio Bicudo and Janaína Paschoal continue their influence in the judiciary and Congress. The polarization sparked by that process continues to shape the 2026 electoral landscape, with Lula and Bolsonaro as central poles.

item.title: Entenda os fatores que levaram ao avanço de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula nas pesquisas
item.description: Recent polls show Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) slightly ahead of Lula (PT) in the 2026 presidential runoff, within the margin of error, due to the transfer of political capital from Jair Bolsonaro, voter fatigue with the current administration, and negative economic perceptions. Despite challenges like low name recognition, Flavio has unified the right-wing electorate and gained ground among independents.

item.title: Lula vai a reunião da esquerda mundial em meio a tensões globais com Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) travels to Barcelona to attend the Global Progressive Mobilisation, a gathering of global left-wing leaders amid rising tensions with Donald Trump. The itinerary includes stops in Germany and Portugal, focusing on threats to democracy, disinformation, and gender-based violence. Analysts view the Spain leg as a political minefield due to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s sharp criticism of U.S. actions and Trump.

item.title: Cadê o ‘Posto Ipiranga’ de Flávio?
item.description: The text questions the delay in announcing Flávio Bolsonaro's promised 'Posto Ipiranga' initiative, comparing it to Paulo Guedes' vague 'next week' rhetoric during his tenure when proposals were stalled by the Centrão. The analogy suggests Flávio seeks someone who could bring him the same credibility Guedes gave to Jair Bolsonaro, but such a figure has not yet emerged. The content is framed as exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Promessa de freio nos gastos em 2027 não convence mercado em meio a ceticismo sobre contas públicas
item.description: The government proposes a strong fiscal adjustment for 2027, limiting total spending growth to just 1% above inflation, after years of averaging 5% above inflation. This reduction relies on factors such as declining judicial rulings, stabilization of the Fundeb, and tight control of personnel spending, which is projected to rise by only R$ 2 billion nominally. Despite government optimism, financial markets remain skeptical, viewing the projections as overly optimistic and warning that the fiscal deficit could be larger than stated.

item.title: Soma das dívidas dos ‘enrolados’ no alvo do novo programa de renegociação pode chegar a R$ 140 bi
item.description: The new debt renegotiation program by the Lula government could cover up to R$ 140 billion in credit card, overdraft, and unsecured personal loans, with delays ranging from 91 days to three years, held by individuals earning up to five minimum wages. The estimate is based on December 2025 data and aims to bring 'delinquent' borrowers back into the financial system. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Governistas articulam jantar entre Lula, Alcolumbre e senadores para destravar apoio a Messias antes de sabatina
item.description: Government allies are organizing a dinner between President Lula, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, and senators to secure support for Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) ahead of his hearing on April 28. The meeting aims to overcome resistance from undecided senators amid a tight calendar, as the Tiradentes holiday will empty Brasília and limit in-person negotiations. Despite progress in talks, many senators remain unwilling to declare their vote publicly, leaving the outcome uncertain as the hearing approaches.

item.title: Entrevista: 'Alguns se tornaram experts em afastar pessoas', diz Nikolas Ferreira após ataques de Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Nikola Ferreira describes his role as an ‘attacker’ whose job is to convey ideas, not just names, in Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre‑campaign. He criticizes Eduardo Bolsonaro’s one‑sided attacks and warns that supporters who act as ‘experts at pushing people away’ hinder outreach.
